A unit with code in another language, such as Rust or Python, no longer reports a measured zero: it has no value and a reason when nothing in it is counted, and otherwise the points of its counted files with a note of what they leave out; a file that is not read has no size either. A reviewed baseline records such a metric as unmeasured instead of a number, later records state it as unavailable and do not judge it, a number that existed at the baseline cannot become unavailable, and a metric that becomes measurable needs a reviewed limit. The count of dependencies is scoped the same way: it covers the units a unit depends on and the outside modules its read files refer to, and it says so when code in another language, packages declared in a manifest such as Cargo.toml, or references that could not be resolved are not in it. entries.behavior: The whole unit as committed, in 3 steps. 40e31b3 (added): Judges one unit: frozen size, complexity and dependencies, and performance only against a baseline with the identical unit, method and comparison context; otherwise incomplete or incompatible. 1d5f793 (<module>, budgetFindings, limited added, sizeFinding, unlimited added, unmeasured added): Complexity is a count only where decision points are counted: TypeScript, JavaScript and Svelte. A unit with code in another language, such as Rust or Python, no longer reports a measured zero: it has no value and a reason when nothing in it is counted, and otherwise the points of its counted files with a note of what they leave out; a file that is not read has no size either. A reviewed baseline records such a metric as unmeasured instead of a number, later records state it as unavailable and do not judge it, a number that existed at the baseline cannot become unavailable, and a metric that becomes measurable needs a reviewed limit. The count of dependencies is scoped the same way: it covers the units a unit depends on and the outside modules its read files refer to, and it says so when code in another language, packages declared in a manifest such as Cargo.toml, or references that could not be resolved are not in it. The measure and status commands, the history index, the component panel and the growth table show the value, the reason or the note. After 1d5f793 (<module>, budgetFindings, frozenFinding added, isFrozen added, sizeFinding removed, unlimited, verdict added): The size of what a unit emits is judged for each execution target against a limit of its own, whenever the unit is judged and not only when its source changed. An output the unit's baseline does not cover is a missing baseline with the detail no-limit-for-output, and one that was measured at the baseline and is gone is a missing measurement. sizeFinding became frozenFinding, which judges any frozen number under the name its limit has in the ledger.

entries.behavior: Complexity is a count only where decision points are counted: TypeScript, JavaScript and Svelte. A unit with code in another language, such as Rust or Python, no longer reports a measured zero: it has no value and a reason when nothing in it is counted, and otherwise the points of its counted files with a note of what they leave out; a file that is not read has no size either. A reviewed baseline records such a metric as unmeasured instead of a number, later records state it as unavailable and do not judge it, a number that existed at the baseline cannot become unavailable, and a metric that becomes measurable needs a reviewed limit. The count of dependencies is scoped the same way: it covers the units a unit depends on and the outside modules its read files refer to, and it says so when code in another language, packages declared in a manifest such as Cargo.toml, or references that could not be resolved are not in it. The measure and status commands, the history index, the component panel and the growth table show the value, the reason or the note. After 1d5f793 (<module>, harnessBudget, limitOf added, noted added, unavailable removed, unreviewed added): A line says frozen at a number only where a reviewed limit is known for the revision: the baseline the record itself judged the value against, else the limit in the ledger of that revision. Without one it says that a freeze is declared and no reviewed limit is recorded there, where it used to say frozen for any measured value. A metric without a value keeps not frozen with its reason, a partial value keeps its note, and a value that exceeded its reviewed limit says what it grew from and to.

simplification.attempt: Until 1d5f793 (not improved): The rule is one function per kind of file and one more case in the judgement of a frozen metric. A declaration in every manifest was considered and dropped: the reviewed ledger already carries the decision. The code grew. After 1d5f793 (improved): One function decides the limit for the three shapes of a line, measured, unavailable and not measured, which removed the separate function for unavailable values; it was split into limitOf and unreviewed after lint measured complexity 11.

performance.attempt: Until 1d5f793 (not applicable): One lookup per owned file per measurement; not measured. After 1d5f793 (not applicable): Not applicable: a few comparisons per shown metric.

A unit with code in another language, such as Rust or Python, no longer reports a measured zero: it has no value and a reason when nothing in it is counted, and otherwise the points of its counted files with a note of what they leave out; a file that is not read has no size either. A reviewed baseline records such a metric as unmeasured instead of a number, later records state it as unavailable and do not judge it, a number that existed at the baseline cannot become unavailable, and a metric that becomes measurable needs a reviewed limit. The count of dependencies is scoped the same way: it covers the units a unit depends on and the outside modules its read files refer to, and it says so when code in another language, packages declared in a manifest such as Cargo.toml, or references that could not be resolved are not in it. The measure and status commands, the history index, the component panel and the growth table show the value, the reason or the note. After 1d5f793 (<module>, BudgetService.failures, describe, subjectOf added, unfrozen added): A failure about an emitted size names its target: growth without approval, an output that is gone since its baseline, an output that became measurable, and an output the baseline of the unit does not cover each say what a reviewer must do. subjectOf words what a finding is about; unfrozen words the two cases of a number that has no limit although the unit has a baseline.

entries.behavior: The whole unit as committed, in 3 steps. 40e31b3 (added): Runs setup and every check inside a clean snapshot, compares the snapshot with the commit after setup and after each check, and refuses an output declaration that covers tracked files. f240fbd (<module>, SnapshotRunService.execute): Ties a capture to compiled files: declared builds are identified in the snapshot by a digest of every file, evidence may name a build, and a capture whose server reported another identity is rejected even when it carries the current revision. The reports server reports the digest of the files it was started from. 1d5f793 (<module>, SnapshotRunService.execute, SnapshotRunService.tools added): A test file may declare a command of its own in harness.verify.json, and declared tools are asked for their version in the snapshot after setup: the record names Harness itself and each tool, and a tool that reports nothing fails the verification before any check runs.
